## Summary

`provision_channels.py` built rooms and then left them half-set-up. This adds the two steps that finish the job — seeding the ops accounts into a chapter's organizer room, and posting that chapter's Drive folder link there. Both gaps were found by auditing the live workspace, not by reading the code.

## Changesets

### 1. `feat(sync-chapters): finish the room — seed ops staff and post the Drive link`

**Ops seed.** 17 of 87 organizer channels — every room provisioned on 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-31 — held neither ops account. Nothing in the repo had ever put them there: the 70 healthy rooms came from a one-off manual pass, so each provisioning run silently reopened the hole. The roster is `Ops staff email` rows on the `Slack Config` tab, resolved by `users.lookupByEmail` (never a `@handle` — its owner can change it). **The addresses are not in this repo**; this repo is public.

**Folder link.** Posted in the **organizer** room, never the public one. The folder holds the CRM, budgets and trackers, so a public link would not leak anything (Drive still refuses everyone else) but would generate Request Access clicks from members who cannot have it — already a recurring support load. The message says so, because the usual cause is being signed into the wrong Google account rather than a missing grant.

**Degrades instead of aborting.** `pins:read`/`pins:write`/`*:history` are in a new `OPTIONAL_SCOPES` and printed when absent; only `channels:write`, `groups:write`, `chat:write` are required. `pins.add` is allowlisted; **`pins.remove` deliberately is not** — unpinning is how a human says "that is no longer the thing to read first".

`write_token()` now falls back to the repo-root `.env` like the read half already did. Without it a run planned fine then failed at the write, and the obvious workaround was exporting the token on the command line — which CLAUDE.md forbids because shell history keeps it.

### 2. `fix(sync-chapters): address self-review findings`

Six review agents; 25 findings, all applied. The four Critical:

- **Duplicate posts into ~80 private rooms.** The idempotency guard was conditional on `pins:read`. `pins.list` answers "is it pinned"; the channel history answers "is it posted", and only the second decides whether to send another message. With `pins:read` granted and `groups:history` absent, every run posted a fresh copy — and granting `pins:read`, which the docstring recommends, is what triggered it. Guard is unconditional.
- **`can_pin` read off the wrong token.** `load_token()` prefers the read var, `write_token()` the write one; the two sweep the same sources in different orders. Scope questions about a write call now go to the write token.
- **Raw sheet cell posted verbatim.** A cell containing `<url|anchor> <!channel>` ahead of a valid folder URL would post as a link with attacker-chosen anchor text under an ops admin's own token. The plan carries the validated id; the URL is rebuilt from it.
- **Apply path discarded the skip list**, so a room created seconds earlier with a bad folder cell was half-configured and appeared nowhere.

Plus a trust boundary on the roster (domain allowlist + size cap), token-owner exclusion (`cant_invite_self` would have pinned the exit code at 1 forever), reported-instead-of-silent handling for token-invisible rooms, and `folder_id` composed from `sync_resources` rather than duplicated.

## Test Plan

- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` clean (ruff, codespell, gitleaks, frontmatter, banner, secret-args, workflows)
- [x] Library suite 386 passed; 40 skill suites passed
- [x] `test_provision_channels.py`: 30 → **67 checks**, including the exact regression and the crafted-cell injection case
- [x] `claude plugin validate .` passed
- [x] CI `validate` green on both commits
- [x] PII scan: only synthetic fixtures; a personal domain that had crept into a comment was removed
- [x] Applied live: 17 rooms seeded, 84 folder links posted, 4 correctly skipped
- [x] Live re-run after the fixes: 87 channels read, 0 pending, idempotent

### Reviewer notes

- **Merge order matters.** The `Slack Config` tab now carries `Ops staff email` and `Ops staff domain` rows that only this branch understands; `load_config` aborts on an unrecognised label.
- The links are already live in 84 channels, posted by the pre-fix code. The currently-deployed scope set (no `pins:read`) is the safe branch, so no duplicates exist — but this must merge **before** `pins:read` is added to the Slack app.
- A test asserts no real address is hardcoded in `provision_channels.py`.
